hero.eyebrow: Independent review · Blueroot Health's four Shopify stores · Sep 28, 2026
headline: Four stores.
One
checklist.
hero.lede: An independent review of Blueroot Health's direct-to-consumer storefronts for the DTC Operations Manager role. I read fairhavenhealth.com in full and sampled bariatricfusion.com, vitalnutrients.co and unjury.com — 397 published products, 57 page fetches, no logins. Fairhaven's public-page baseline is the strongest I have measured this year. The six findings below are the operating gaps a weekly QA sheet would catch: empty footer collections, a sold-out product in the #2 slot sitewide, a 30%-off badge with no discounted price, facts panels that exist only as JPGs, titles that truncate on every product page, and four stores with four sets of rules from one warehouse.

why.title: Why Blueroot Health
why.sub: The posting asks for someone who keeps four storefronts “accurate, performant and conversion-ready” with “a documented, repeatable operating cadence.” I read the stores the way that person would on a Monday morning.
rows: Collections, navigation, sort defaults, promotions — findings 1, 2 and 3.
Titles, descriptions, attributes, schema, facts panels — findings 4 and 5.
A repeatable cadence across the portfolio
Policy pages, shipping promises, shared-SKU naming across four stores — finding 6.
Every finding is a row in the QA workbook that ships with this page.
why.note: Everything here comes from public pages and Shopify's public product feeds (products.json, collections.json). I evaluated structure, data and merchandising only — no health or product claim language, which belongs to your regulatory review, not mine.

strengths.title: A clean technical-SEO baseline on Fairhaven
strengths.text: robots.txt ends with the sitemap line; every one of 20 sampled product pages has a self-referencing canonical, a unique title, a unique description and Product + Offer JSON-LD with sku and gtin12; 17 of 20 also carry FAQPage schema.

strengths.title: Real, metafield-driven discovery
strengths.text: Collection filters run on custom metafields — gender, life stage, health benefit, key ingredients, made without, product form, FSA/HSA eligibility — with nine sort options, and site search returns a proper results page with the same filters. Bariatric Fusion and Vital Nutrients use the same approach.

strengths.title: One PDP template, and prices that agree everywhere
strengths.text: All 20 sampled Fairhaven PDPs share one template (benefits, ingredients, use, description, FAQ, bought-together) with Stamped reviews and Recharge subscribe-and-save. Card price = PDP price = feed price on 20 of 20 Fairhaven, 40 of 40 Bariatric Fusion and 16 of 16 Vital Nutrients products checked; the 89 SKUs shared by bariatricfusion.com and unjury.com show 0 price and 0 stock mismatches.

findings.title: Footer “Shop” links and the sitemap point at empty collections
findings.count: 3 of 8 footer collection links · 4 of 42 sitemap collections · 32 products vs 42 collections
findings.observed: The footer's “Pregnancy” link opens /collections/shop-pregnancy, which renders “No products found” under a title that still promises stretch mark cream and fetal dopplers — and the page is indexable and in the sitemap. “Pregnancy and Ovulation Tests” is empty too; “Ovulation Prediction” holds exactly one product, the sold-out BabyDance lubricant. collections.json still reports counts of 120, 74 and 45 for collections that hold unpublished legacy items, against a storefront of 32 published products.
findings.why: The posting's first duty is collections, navigation and “routine QA checks for broken links and content discrepancies.” A footer link to zero products is the purchase-path dead end that role exists to catch.
findings.fix: Unpublish shop-pregnancy, pregnancy-products, pregnancy-and-ovulation-tests, private, uncategorized and fairhaven-health from the Online Store channel so they leave the sitemap; retitle the survivors; repoint the footer “Pregnancy” link to /collections/prenatal and remove “Ovulation Prediction”; run the collection-health check below every Monday.

findings.title: A sold-out product is the #2 item on All Products and in the search drawer sitewide
findings.count: position 2 of 32 on /collections/all · position 2 of 3 in “Trending Now” on 32 of 32 captured pages
findings.observed: /collections/all defaults to Alphabetically, A–Z, so BabyDance Fertility Lubricant — the only fully sold-out product in products.json — sits second with a Sold out badge. The theme's search drawer shows the first three A–Z products as “Trending Now” on every page, so the sold-out item is the second trending product on the homepage, the contact page, every policy page and every PDP. vitalnutrients.co's All Products defaults to A–Z as well.
findings.why: The first screen of All Products and the search drawer are the two highest-traffic merchandising slots on the store, and both lead with something nobody can buy.
findings.fix: Set All Products to Best selling (or manual with sold-out last); turn on “push sold-out to the bottom” in Search & Discovery; point the theme's Trending Now block at a curated collection; add the available flag from products.json to the weekly QA sheet so any sold-out SKU in a top-8 slot is flagged.

findings.title: “30% OFF – select sizes” badges on single-variant products while every price still shows full
findings.count: 5 of 32 products badged · 5 of 5 single-variant · 0 of 5 show a reduced price · 0 of 32 use compare-at pricing
findings.observed: A badge reading “30% OFF · LIMITED-TIME OFFER · SELECT SIZES – APPLIED IN CART” sits on five product cards and PDPs. All five products have one variant (“Default Title”), so “select sizes” cannot apply. Because the discount is an automatic in-cart discount, the card, the PDP price ($26.99 for FertileCM), the Offer.price in JSON-LD and the Recharge subscription price (10% off the full price) all show the undiscounted number. compare_at_price is null on 32 of 32 Fairhaven products — and on 112 of 112 Bariatric Fusion, 167 of 168 Vital Nutrients and 85 of 85 UNJURY products — so no store ever shows a strike-through sale price.
findings.why: “Pricing issues” and “promotions” are explicit QA duties, and an Offer.price that differs from the checkout price is a Merchant Center and Shop app mismatch waiting to be flagged.
findings.fix: Run the promotion as compare-at pricing on the affected variants (bulk editor) or as a Shopify Functions discount surfaced in the theme's price block so badge, price and JSON-LD agree; make the badge copy conditional on variant count; adopt a five-step promo launch check — badge → price display → JSON-LD → subscription price → cart total — on one badged PDP before go-live.

findings.title: Supplement Facts live only in JPGs; product_type and tags are unusable for merchandising
findings.count: facts panel image-only on 17 of 20 PDPs · Ingredients accordion ≤19 words on 15 of 20 · product_type blank on 32 of 32 · 32 tags on 32 products
findings.observed: On 17 of 20 sampled Fairhaven PDPs the facts panel is a gallery image; no PDP has an HTML table, and the Ingredients accordion on 15 of 20 holds only the other-ingredients line (8–19 words). products.json shows product_type blank on all 32 products (Bariatric Fusion: 0 of 112 blank), 32 distinct tags on 32 products including three spellings of one concept and internal flags (exclude_rebuy, fam-fhpro-men, Ovia, The Ribbon Box) mixed with merchandising tags. One product ships with an empty description, no facts image and no subscription widget.
findings.why: Product attributes, SKU-level monitoring and feeds all key off product_type and tags, and text that exists only inside a JPG cannot be searched, filtered or read by a screen reader.
findings.fix: Add a custom.supplement_facts metafield and render it as a table inside the Ingredients accordion (keep the image as a second view); set Shopify's standard Product Category plus a house product_type list on all 32 products via CSV; move internal flags to a custom.internal_flags metafield and collapse the three vaginal-care tags into one; a products.json diff before and after is the acceptance test.

findings.title: Every sampled PDP title truncates in search; no rating or breadcrumb schema; no H1 on the homepage
findings.count: 20 of 20 titles at 73–91 characters · 13 of 20 descriptions end “Learn more…” · 0 of 20 with aggregateRating · 0 of 20 with BreadcrumbList · 20 of 20 og:image over http
findings.observed: Each product title carries a benefit clause plus “ – Fairhaven Health” (the longest is 91 characters), so Google cuts all 20. The homepage has no h1 or h2 — the hero line “A Better Prenatal for the First 1000 Days” is not a heading. Product JSON-LD has no aggregateRating on 20 of 20 PDPs even though the Stamped badge on the same page exposes the review count and rating, and no Fairhaven or Bariatric Fusion PDP has BreadcrumbList (Vital Nutrients does). The homepage copy also contains “clincially-tested.”
findings.why: The posting asks for on-page SEO, content scorecards and organic search visibility; these are the cheapest measurable wins on the digital shelf.
findings.fix: Rewrite titles to ≤60 characters with the product first and the brand last (bulk editor or the search-engine-listing field) and replace the “Learn more…” tail; wrap the hero headline in an h1; enable Stamped's rich-snippet JSON-LD; add a BreadcrumbList snippet to main-product.liquid; set the social image URL to https. Track title length and schema presence per SKU in the weekly scorecard.

findings.title: Four stores, four conventions: policies, shipping promises and shared-SKU names diverge
findings.count: 4 themes · 4 policy-URL patterns · 3 free-shipping thresholds ($35 / $49 / $100) from one warehouse · 28 of 89 shared SKUs titled differently · 1 live “copy-of-” handle + 5 “-1” handles · 7 empty descriptions on Vital Nutrients
findings.observed: The four stores run four themes and put shipping, terms and contact pages at four URL patterns. All four ship from 45 Kenneth Dooley Drive, yet free shipping starts at $35 (Fairhaven), $49 (Vital Nutrients) and $100 (Bariatric Fusion), processing is “1–2” vs “within 2” business days and delivery “4–8” vs “3–5.” bariatricfusion.com and unjury.com sell 89 identical SKUs with matching prices and stock but 28 different titles for the same SKU. Bariatric Fusion still serves a product at a copy-of- handle published in 2020 with a 5% subscription discount (10% elsewhere), plus five -1 duplicate handles and two empty collections; seven Vital Nutrients products — six of them the kids line launched in June 2026 — have an empty body_html, so feeds carry no description.
findings.why: The role is defined as “a documented, repeatable operating cadence across the portfolio.” These are the places where one owner and one checklist would show up immediately.
findings.fix: Publish a one-page portfolio standard (policy handles, free-shipping copy, processing and transit language taken from the 3PL's real SLA, subscription discount) and align each store to it; keep a master SKU sheet (SKU → canonical title → price → subscription %) and reconcile bariatricfusion.com and unjury.com by CSV; rename the copy-of and -1 handles with 301 redirects; copy the kids-line section copy into body_html so Shop and Google feeds get a description.

also: /collections/all has no meta description (Shopify default); nav collections do.
PDP breadcrumb is only Home / product (no collection level) while collection pages show Home / Shop / collection.
The Rebuy bought-together widget exposes live inventory counts in a hidden select (data-qty="15816" for FH PRO for Men).
complete-menopause-relief renders an empty 0.0 Stamped badge on cards and PDP instead of hiding it.
Multi-variant cards (myo-inositol $19.99 / $35.99) show one price with no “From.”
Blog index and homepage blog cards carry no publish dates.
Fairhaven's newest published_at is 2026-01-28; Vital Nutrients published six kids SKUs in May–June 2026 and UNJURY's newest is 2026-07-28.
